description.value: Primitive backcountry camping in Babine Mountains Provincial Park near Smithers, set among glacier-fed lakes, rugged peaks, and vast sub-alpine meadows; the west-end road is closed to vehicles beyond the parking lot so access is trail-only, and all water must be treated on site.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record points to Babine Mountains Park, a BC Parks provincial park near Smithers. The website confirms this is backcountry/primitive camping requiring hiking access from trailheads off Highway 16 — the road is 'not passable to vehicle traffic' beyond the parking lot. The website explicitly states water from natural sources must be boiled or treated, confirming no potable water. Bears (grizzly and black) are present. The Cronin Pass route mentions bikers as permitted users, but the camping itself is wilderness backcountry with no facilities mentioned.
concerns: Name 'Primitive Camping' is a generic descriptor, not a proper place name
Access requires leaving Highway 16 and hiking in from trailhead parking — not roadside or bicycle-accessible camping
Grizzly and black bear habitat — no mention of food storage facilities
No address, phone, or on-site contact available
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is primitive backcountry camping in a mountain park requiring hiking access from trailheads — the road is impassable to vehicles beyond the parking lot. Not readily accessible by touring bicycle and offers no facilities. May not serve WWC directory users unless the directory includes backcountry options for bikepacking-style cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: Closest communities are Smithers and Telkwa on Highway 16. The Cronin Pass route (26.7 km) permits bikers, but this is mountain biking/bikepacking terrain, not road touring.
